notes.title: Project: Werwolf Dev Blog #6 Caves
notes.notes:
Greetings Hunter,

Welcome to our new developer blog! This post will be a bit shorter as we’re currently working on an exciting new feature. Let me show you what’s coming.

Our upcoming feature introduces Caves—yes, caves! Scattered throughout the map, these caves are home to werewolves. Inside, you’ll find not only packs of werewolves but also nests of the Black Plague and key items that will aid you on your journey as a Hunter. There are small caves associated with specific points of interest, such as the mine, and larger, more dangerous caves that serve as the hearts of the nests. Destroying these nests will significantly reduce the number of werewolves in the area and gradually weaken their strength, making it easier for you to fight back and cleanse the world of these creatures. Once you fully clear a cave, it becomes "cleansed," allowing you to freely harvest its mineral resources. We strongly recommend coming well-prepared, as you never know what dangers might await—and whether you’ll emerge alive!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/abbc4011b763bb21a23a525c7c45ee343d916725.png[/img]

The cave system is our major development focus at the moment, and there is still much work to be done. We’ll share more insights as the system evolves.

Now, onto our next point: the drug laboratory.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/1edaca6627f47a28d0814562e188ce180086f91d.png[/img]

This new point of interest is located on the outskirts of the map. Here, you can find various chemical compounds to craft new medicines, cure infections, or even explore other possibilities. It also serves as a safe haven, offering a space where you can build your home—even though it might not be my first choice.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/7bf257c977ec04ee29073cc872d80b8a9d6163ee.png[/img]

That’s all for now. Though this update is a bit shorter than usual, our aim is to develop something truly unique and engaging that offers new ways to play and experience Project: Werewolf.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/54eb64c34b68a4e728779af9b9b2dcf901c1d2b1.png[/img]

Until next time, Hunter. Cheers!

notes.title: Project: Werwolf Dev Blog #5 Engine Update and Cabins
notes.notes:
Upgrade to Unreal Engine 5.5
With the latest version of Unreal Engine, we have access to a range of new features that make the game world more immersive, realistic, and dynamic. One of the biggest additions is Mega Light, a groundbreaking technology that allows us to use a vast number of dynamic light sources—without significantly impacting performance.

Previously, we often had to limit the number of light sources to maintain a stable frame rate. This was especially noticeable indoors, where cabins, houses, and even streetlights had to be designed with fewer lights. But with Mega Light, that’s no longer a problem. Now, we can fully utilize atmospheric lighting to create dense, immersive environments. Whether it's flickering candles in an abandoned cabin, softly glowing streetlights, or the eerie glow of a fire pit—all these details can now be fully realized to enhance the world’s atmosphere.

Another exciting feature is Skeletal Mesh Tessellation, which allows for real-time deformation of organic creatures. This means we can introduce more lifelike animations and believable creature behavior. Muscles and skin will react dynamically to movement, wounds or deformities can be realistically displayed, and even fine surface details can adapt in real-time. How exactly we’ll use this feature in the game? Stay tuned for a future dev blog!

New Cabins and Houses
Creating a dynamic and ever-changing experience is one of our main goals. That’s why we've been working on an advanced procedural system that not only generates cabins and houses but also fills them with realistic interiors.

The core of this system isn’t just random object placement—it’s about structured, believable interior design. Our goal is to make procedurally generated buildings indistinguishable from handcrafted level designs. To achieve this, we use different procedural construction methods depending on the type of building:

Cabins: The interiors of cabins are generated as open, interconnected spaces. This results in organic and natural environments that perfectly suit smaller dwellings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/f821040fcbbb236736ebe3b6fc9f8f9868147e43.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/b561f4e312362b3389f084536908c03453481109.png[/img]

Houses: Unlike cabins, houses are divided into multiple rooms, each with a distinct function (e.g., living room, bedroom, kitchen, dining area). We use a category-specific procedural generation (PCG) system to ensure logical furniture placement.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/5da20a84a30869f6a55299027d43371e9fae4f1d.png[/img]

Each room type follows specific design principles to create a cohesive and immersive environment. For example, sofas in a living room aren’t just placed randomly; they form realistic seating arrangements around a table or fireplace. Dining rooms feature well-organized layouts with tables, chairs, and cabinets, while bedrooms have logically positioned beds, nightstands, and wardrobes.


Balancing Procedural Generation and Handcrafted Design:


A fully procedurally generated world runs the risk of feeling too chaotic or random. That’s why we’re carefully balancing procedural variety with handcrafted elements.

To ensure structure, each world will feature fixed, handcrafted landmarks that act as anchor points. These unique locations tell their own stories and provide a strong contrast to the procedurally generated environments. Players can use these points as recognizable landmarks, helping them navigate even as the world changes around them.

This blend of procedural dynamism and carefully placed handcrafted elements ensures that the game world feels fresh and unique with every playthrough—while maintaining a consistent atmosphere and sense of coherence.

And that wraps up this Dev Blog.

Stay tuned for more updates, and as always, happy hunting!

notes.title: Project: Werwolf Dev Blog #4 A new year and the Watchtower
notes.notes:
Greetings Hunters!

First of all happy new year to you. We hope you arrived well in 2025, and welcome to our first dev update this year!

Now we come to the more important stuff happening at Evolve games. Most of you know we at the studio are just 2 main developers working on Project werewolf and we had a lot of difficulty in the last quarter of 2024 especially in our real life. Because of that we stopped development around mid of october till now. We had a lot of workload to finish and of course the holiday seasons, where we just recharged our batteries to start fresh in 2025. We are sorry we went dark so sudden but sometimes life can be hard. Now that we resumed development, we want to talk about new stuff.

Secondly, we want to introduce the new watchtowers! The watchtowers are a central point of safety in the night, where you can safely rest and equip yourself. No werewolf can attack you up there and you can even upgrade them to make small little stations to refill your supplies, sleep through the night, or just decorate how you want. You first need to claim and “unlock” them. The watchtowers are built to make exploration easier at night, so you won't need to return to your own fortified home.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/ed99f8f147add3e9179f019fe30cbcc0f7d572fb.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/010e0a578e36e3256082c2ec675b4c97902fdc83.png[/img]

Watchtowers are scattered all around the map and have different designs. They are handbuilt to make them as immersive as possible, but we still want to give you the freedom to decorate them however you want. But more about that in a future post!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/4337e6af2ff86dd23422a7518b5aeec470223ef5.png[/img]

Second of all, we did a lot of backend changes to coding and fixed a whole lot of bugs. We also built some small corrugated iron houses for a new POI I'm currently working on. Can you guess what it will be? We will reveal the POI in our next dev blog, so no worries if you can't guess it right. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/fd72053ab2fa0d498cd92675dc060cfceda84faa.png[/img]

During our inactive period, we weren't entirely idle! We're excited to share that, in addition to Project Werewolf, a smaller game is also in development. This project provides us with a great opportunity to test additional mechanics, which will ultimately benefit Project Werewolf as well.

Undead Awakens is a small, round-based zombie survival coop shooter that we plan to release soon but won't impact werewolf's development at all since only half of the team develop it in their free time. You can currently wishlist it and we plan to have a playtest soon to gather some community wishes. The money from the sales we get will be redirected to Project Werewolf and will help to enhance it more.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3291340/Undead_Awakens/

With that, we close the first dev blog of 2025 and we at Evolve Games want to thank you so much for sticking with us and giving us so much support. Since we are now in full force of development, you can expect more frequent updates and even a playtest in the near future. 

With that, we see you next month, Hunters!!

notes.title: Project: Werwolf Dev Blog #3 Orientation and dangers
notes.notes:
Welcome, Hunters!

In this third installment of our Dev Blog, we will delve into three significant aspects of the game: the Cathedral, the Smartwatch, and the ominous Black Plague.

The Cathedral:

The Cathedral serves as the central landmark on the map, prominently situated on a massive hill.
It is the foundation around which every Point of Interest (POI) is constructed, allowing players to navigate and explore the surroundings with ease.
However, be cautious! The Cathedral is heavily affected by the Black Plague, creating an environment filled with danger.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/f74e7ef3a9a372ffa81a6e5497d6179cf845c13f.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/6affc55582eb8fd3523712997bb6a2637f9154a4.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/f1e86a00fee1b322befe266883ea2b1360dd3138.png[/img]

What is the Black Plague?

The Black Plague refers to a toxic mushroom that proliferates across the game world, particularly in caves.
This mushroom is hazardous; prolonged exposure can lead to permanent damage to your character.

The Smartwatch:

The innovative Smartwatch replaces the traditional HUD, offering players a more immersive experience.
Key features of the Smartwatch include:
Health, Food, Water, and Sanity indicators.
Displays time, weather, and temperature.
Monitors your status, alerting you if you are infected or suffering from any ailments.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/413f1848493b9d3e3be13af530237273e2ad759b.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/47b4ae7999718fa9a511e18c96d4913a4f19a325.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/2df1343fb8d82b9787167263dada1193d62805d5.gif[/img]

As a special treat, we are excited to share a glimpse of the new procedurally generated cabins that will enhance your gameplay experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/adfe2d252a219abd68865943d741383c644fd40e.png[/img] 

We will provide more about the procedural cabins and houses in a following dev blog.

Conclusion:

Thank you for joining us in this update, Hunters! We hope you found the information exciting and informative. Stay tuned for our next blog post next month. Until then, remember to stay safe, seek shelter at night, and prepare for the challenges that lie ahead. Something big may be on the horizon!

Until next time! 

Evolve Games

notes.title: Dev-Blog #2 Wildlife and Inventory
notes.notes:
Greeting Hunters,

Welcome to the second dev blog of Project Werewolf.
Today, we want to talk a little bit about wildlife, forests, and food sources in combination with our inventory system. 

Firstly, we want to talk about the forests because we have a quite unique open world. The forests and all around them are procedurally generated, from small cabins (More in a future post) to how the wildlife behaves and which animals spawn at which biome. 

Everything will be random once you start a new game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/0667615a0079a51ab58e7ea2fc3e0ed82d0192f8.png[/img]

The same spot with another seed

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/d40c4a5cfb63cae0e4e498a23b3b7298a42e8465.png[/img]

Even the potential food is different, from berries to herbs or trees with fruits on them. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/dc139971b1c9e39ce73974442e215591bc54068a.png[/img]

Big POI's like the Farm or the Cathedral are not procedurally generated; they are handmade and will exist in every save game.  You are free to use it as orientation! Our goal is to create a memorable, open world that tells our story but also changes once you begin a new game or you join your friends, so you always have something to explore and something new to find.

Now onto the inventory system. We chose a more realistic approach to the inventory system.
Upon starting the game, you have a backpack that uses a 3D tile placement system. Every item has a unique tile size that needs enough space in the backpack to fit properly. This ensures that a big part of a survival game, inventory management, won't be too easy yet also fits the immersion of a more realistic survival game. 


You can rotate items:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/14b52457f042fc7f33cc30fc23e59c002ce4690c.gif[/img]

And you can seamless equip gear:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/790ec8ce06e4d528b5c8a01ac5ccf3029ce95ef8.gif[/img]

Later on, you can use storage to store everything you want to keep. We are also working on a car system with a “trunk” inventory system so you can transport more resources with you. But more about this in a future post.

That's all for now, hunters. We hope you liked this dev blog, and we would appreciate your feedback and support according to the inventory system and the procedural part. Do you have any ideas or suggestions? Let us know in the forum or join our [url=https://discord.gg/ymCcpySQmC]Discord[/url].

See you next time,
Evolve games

notes.title: Dev-Blog #1 Project: Werewolf
notes.notes:
Welcome to our first ever dev blog on Project Werewolf. Our plan is to drop a new dev blog every month to keep you up to date on everything we are working on.

We want to talk about the current state of Project werewolf and what's already done or will be finished in the next few weeks. But keep in mind, everything we are showing is still in progress. 

Firstly, we have a fully fleshed-out POI called The Farm. The Farm is supposed to be the starting point for your journey Project: Werewolf, and the first spot you will explore and let you experience the game. We aim to give every POI something special, so you always have to go back and check if you missed something. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/a4199a5657833859eab6213981d5d30d08835ae2.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/10feceecffdfedcb7f10cf324bb2a272f4d2ca8f.png[/img]


Secondly we want to talk about the Werewolfs the key aspect of the game. Werewolfs are the main threat in Project: Werewolf that will react to you and have different behaviors depending on how you play and how you progress throughout the game. They will frequently scout for you at night but keep in mind the caves are nearly empty. This is a perfect opportunity to discover the secrets of the cave systems. On the other hand, during the day, you can find shelter, food, and weapons to prepare for the hunt. But be aware, exploring caves at daytime is to your own risk. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/e0ddbb59c584be153ffc9db243fe9b3dc6364d78.png[/img]

The main goal is to balance the AI and adapt it to your playstyle while trying to make them less annoying. In addition, the game will have full moon cycles where the Werewolfs are highly aggressive and even stronger at. Be prepared for this challenge.

In the last part, we want to talk about our gun system. Our goal with the gun system is to make it as realistic as possible and to feel smooth. To achieve that, the weapons will have realistic procedural recoil which influences the player arms. You need to master these different recoil patterns on different guns, and adapt your loadout to the environment. And weapons can also jam; the more damaged the gun is, the higher is the chance for miss functions. With this system, we ensure a realistic experience while also giving you the choice to use melee or ranged based on your play style.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/7c65b1a05e1b710e4432d0df09378c7ada5e1eb2.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44998542/50f2d23ee469e709b24d27ab59609ac7f604a50e.gif[/img]

With all that said, we want to close this first dev blog now. You can join our [url=https://discord.gg/ymCcpySQmC]Discord[/url] to become involved in future updates, playtests, and early builds of the game. 

See you next month, 

Evolve Games
